## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vicayahāravibhaṅga* is an analytical chapter belonging to the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Netti) in the late Pali canonical and para-canonical corpus [SuttaCentral]. It forms the opening division of the *Hāravibhaṅga* ("separate treatment of conveying modes"), which initiates the *paṭiniddesa* ("counter-demonstrative subsection", Nett 5,14–193,2), the main body of the work [von Hinüber 1996]. Within the hermeneutical method of the text, *vicayahāra* denotes "investigation" or "conveying investigation", defined epistemologically as the procedure of explicating a passage by means of its verbal meaning [Khemananda 1993; SuttaCentral]. Structurally, the *hāravibhaṅga* takes each mnemonic summary verse from the earlier *niddesavāra* and unpacks it through extensive citations and doctrinal illustrations drawn from the Suttapiṭaka, concluding with the traditional attribution formula affirming that this is why the Venerable Mahākaccāna spoke [von Hinüber 1996]. Textual variants on the opening page (Nett 5.23) have also been discussed in philological treatments of early Buddhist poetry such as the *Sutta Nipāta* [Norman 1997–2001].
SuttaCentral registers an internal parallel to the *Catubyūhahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 9) and cross-references related treatments in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1, Pe 5) as well as the *Ajitamāṇavapucchā* (Snp 5.2) and its canonical commentaries (*Cūḷaniddesa*, Cnd 2 and Cnd 5) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus corroborates extensive Pali-internal text reuse (1,457 matching segments across 104 texts), showing massive overlap with commentaries and sub-commentaries such as the *Nettivibhāvinī* and *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as high-similarity alignments with Canonical texts including the *Cūḷaniddesa* (Cnd 5), *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51), *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 8), *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Samaṇamuṇḍika Sutta* (MN 78), and *Sodhanahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 16) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic alignments with Sanskrit works including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and *Ekottarāgama*, and Chinese Āgama texts such as the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
